newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens wins 270 mln dmk U.S. plant order.
newsitem.headline: Siemens wins 270 mln dmk U.S. plant order.

text.p: German electronics and engineering giant Siemens AG said on Wednesday that it had won a 270 million mark ($173 million) order to build a combined-cycle power plant in the state of Missouri, U.S.
Siemens said in a statement that the plant would be built by the Siemens Power Generation Group (KWU), and that the order included a long-term operation and service contract.

The plant will be based near the city of St Francis and operated by independent power producer Associated Electric Cooperative Inc, which will feed around 250 megawatts into the grid once commercial operation begins in 1999, Siemens said.
Siemens said the plant would be equipped with a 170-megawatt Model V84.3A gas turbine, which would give an efficiency of over 58 percent -- the highest of all combined cycle power plants in the U.S.
"In view of the extraordinarily low volume of contract awards currently being placed in the U.S., it (the order) is of particular significance for the company," Siemens said.
The order means the total orders booked for Siemens/KWU's third generation of gas turbines has risen to 69, of which 43 will be provisionally on line by the end of 1996, the statement added.
